london_system.name: London System
london_system.summary: A solid, easy-to-learn opening. You play the same setup almost every game. Bishop out before e3 — that's the golden rule.
golden_rules: Bishop to f4 BEFORE e3. Always.
Don't trade your dark bishop unless you get something big.
Your dream setup: d4, e3, Bf4, Nf3, Bd3, O-O. Memorize it.
After setup is done, push for e4 — that's your middlegame goal.

traps.name: Englund Gambit Trap
traps.description: They play 1...e5 trying to trick you. Don't fall for it — take the pawn and win.
traps.trap_idea: They try to grab your b2 pawn. Let them — then trap their queen.
traps.how_to_set: Just play normal development. Their queen gets stuck.
traps.avoid_as_white: Don't panic when they check. Bd2 blocks and develops.

traps.name: Bg4 Pin Trick
traps.description: They pin your knight with Bg4. You have a strong response.
traps.trap_idea: Push g4 to kick their bishop, then jump Ne5 attacking everything.
traps.how_to_set: When they play Bg4, don't panic. h3 then g4 is strong.
traps.avoid_as_white: Only play g4 if your king is safe or you've already castled queenside.

traps.name: Queen Trap after c5
traps.description: They play c5 early and you can win a pawn with a trick.
traps.trap_idea: They take b2 with their queen. Nb5 threatens Nc7 fork and Rb1 traps the queen.
traps.how_to_set: Let them take b2. It looks free but their queen has no escape.
traps.avoid_as_white: Make sure you have Nb5 available before allowing Qxb2.

d4.idea: Take the center. This is your territory.
d4.plan: Next move: get your bishop to f4. That's the London identity.

d5.name: Main Line
d5.idea_opponent: They take their share of the center. Fair game.
d5.next_idea: THE London move. Bishop comes out BEFORE e3. If you play e3 first, the bishop is stuck forever.

Nf6.name: London Classical
Nf6.idea_opponent: Developing and aiming at your e4 square.
Nf6.next_idea: Now you lock in the solid center. d4+e3 is a wall.

e6.name: Solid Setup
e6.next_idea: Develop the knight. Aims at e5 — a great square.
e6.plan: Finish development: Bd3, O-O, then push for e4.

c5.name: Center Challenge
c5.next_idea: Support d4. Don't let them break your center.
c5.plan: After c3, develop Nbd2. Your plan is to push e4 when ready.

Bd6.name: Bishop Trade Offer
Bd6.next_idea: Step back. Don't trade your bishop — it's your best piece.
Bd6.plan: If they take on g3, you open the h-file for your rook. Attack!

Be7.name: Quiet Development
Be7.next_idea: Point your bishop at h7. Classic attacking setup.
Be7.plan: O-O, then Nbd2-e5 or push e4. You're in great shape.

c5.name: Early c5 Push
c5.next_idea: Hold the center. Don't panic about c5.
c5.plan: They want to break your d4. c3 holds it. Then Nf3, Bd3, O-O.

Nc6.plan: Bd3, O-O, then e4 is your dream.

Qb6.name: Queen Attack on b2
Qb6.next_idea: Trade queens or protect b2. Either way you're fine.
Qb6.plan: If they trade queens, you get a great endgame. If not, you develop freely.
Qb6.warning: Don't let them take b2 unless you have the Nb5 trick ready.

Bg4.name: Bishop Pin
Bg4.next_idea: Develop anyway. The pin isn't dangerous yet.
Bg4.plan: Play h3 to ask the bishop what it wants. If Bh5, you can push g4 later.

c5.name: Immediate c5
c5.next_idea: Solidify. Don't rush to defend d4 — it's fine.
c5.plan: After e3, play c3 if needed, then develop normally. They can't really break d4.

Nc6.next_idea: Extra support for d4. Now it's rock solid.
Nc6.plan: Nf3, Bd3, O-O. Standard London setup. You're fine.

Qb6.next_idea: Develop and set up the b2 trap.
Qb6.warning: If they take b2, you have Nb5 and Rb1 — their queen is dead.

Bf5.name: Mirror London
Bf5.idea_opponent: Copying your idea! Bishop out before e6.
Bf5.next_idea: Stick to the plan. Your setup still works.
Bf5.plan: Nf3, Bd3 (offer to trade bishops), c4 (challenge their center). You have more space.

Nf6.name: Indian Setup
Nf6.idea_opponent: Flexible — could go King's Indian or Queen's Indian.
Nf6.next_idea: Same plan. Bishop out first, always.

g6.name: King's Indian vs London
g6.next_idea: Solid center. They'll fianchetto — that's fine.
g6.plan: Nf3, Bd3, O-O. Against the fianchetto, your bishop on f4 controls e5. Plant a knight there.

e6.name: Transpose to Main Line
e6.next_idea: We're back to the main London. Same plan.
e6.plan: Nf3, Bd3, O-O, c3, Nbd2, e4.

d5.name: Delayed d5
d5.next_idea: Same as the main line. They just played Nf6 first.

f5.name: Dutch Defense
f5.idea_opponent: Aggressive — they want to attack your kingside.
f5.next_idea: Stay calm. Your London setup handles this well.
f5.plan: e3, Nf3, Bd3. Their kingside is weak because of f5. You can exploit e5 and the holes.

e6.name: Passive Response
e6.idea_opponent: Very passive. Locks in their light bishop.
e6.next_idea: You're already better. They made the bishop-lock mistake.
e6.plan: Standard setup. You have more space and better development.

c5.name: Benoni Style
c5.next_idea: Grab space. Now it's a Benoni-like structure where you have more room.
c5.plan: Bf4, e3 (or e4 if possible), Nf3. You have a space advantage.

when_ahead.plan: Push e4 to open the center. Trade off their defensive pieces. Use your space.
ideas: Push e4 when your pieces are ready
Trade bishops if it opens lines for your rooks
Put a knight on e5 — it's a monster there

when_equal.plan: Aim for e4 push. If that's not possible, play on the queenside with a4-a5 or switch to kingside with h4-h5.
ideas: If e4 isn't possible, try to open another file
Keep your dark bishop — it's your best piece

when_behind.plan: Keep the position closed. Your solid structure d4+e3 is hard to break. Wait for their mistake.
ideas: Don't panic — the London is solid
Look for tactical tricks on the kingside
Trade queens if you can — your endgame structure is usually good

kingside_attack.plan: Bd3 aims at h7. Knight to e5. Push h4-h5 if they castled kingside.
ideas: Bd3 + knight on e5 = classic battery
h4 push can open the h-file
If their dark bishop is gone, your f4 bishop is king

endgame_tips: Your pawn structure (d4+e3) is very solid in endgames.
If you still have your dark bishop, it controls important squares.
Push your passed pawns. The London gives you a good pawn structure for endgames.
King to e2-d3 quickly in endgames — centralize.
